'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by style who has placed three times in 15 similar-ground runs without winning; Connor Beasley returns on a horse in decent nick after just 10 days, and his good-ground 6f record (3/6f/GOO, 2/6f/GOO) makes him one of the better poised runners if he can get a position close enough to the pace.|

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6-year-old has struggled for form recently, posting placings in only 3 of 15 similar-ground starts with zero wins; Amie Waugh's 3lb claim barely offsets the poor recent string, and at 21 days since last run with a 13th on the same course type, enthusiasm is hard to find.|

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field and therefore the pivotal tactical horse in this race; Mark Winn must press on from the stalls and control a solo lead, which is very achievable given the field has no true challenger for the front, though the step up from 5f to 6f is worth noting given five of the last six runs have been over shorter.|

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: W H Harrison's 3-year-old has back-to-back seconds over 5f on good ground and is the yard's only runner in the 14-day window from just 2 runners — limited trainer data but the form trend is upward; the step to 6f is unproven but the horse's profile as a close-prominet type suits the expected race shape well.|

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground last season and that course-going combination is clearly her best medium; Katie Scott's filly is a genuine hold-up runner whose natural position at the rear will be harder to express in a race lacking strong pace — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 is worth respecting, meaning her winning chance depends on others' errors more than her own ability.|

runners_data.name: Joshuas Dream
runners_data.note: Lauren Young's 5lb claim is the headline here, but the form string — including a 12th and 17th — makes the statistical case hard; a true hold-up type whose preferred patient style is unlikely to be rewarded in what shapes up as a controlled-pace race, and the redistribution away from her natural position reflects that structural mismatch.|

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Headgear is noted (hg:h) and Tom Eaves is a positive booking, but a blank record in 6 similar-ground starts (0W0P) tells a stark story; naturally races from the rear and has been mapped to midfield purely because of overcrowding at the back — in a race likely set at a sustainable tempo, generating a winning late run will be a tall order.|

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners a horse whose last five runs span 7f to 10f — the return to 6f looks like a major query on trip grounds; a genuine hold-up type with 0W2P in 15 similar-ground starts, mapped into midfield on the chart because the field is stacked at the rear, and the shorter trip adds an extra layer of doubt.|

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: James Sullivan rides the lowest-weighted runner in the race, and Lanarra has a win and multiple placings including a recent 2nd and 3rd over 6f on good and soft — the form line is genuinely solid for a low-rated 3-year-old; a natural hold-up runner whose best chance materialises if the pace quickens enough to open a late gap, with the close weight advantage over older rivals worth noting.|

races.paceDynamic: Water Of Leith is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 9-runner 6f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good-to-firm ground at Ayr. The pace note flags that Falcon Queen, Joshuas Dream, Cotai Starlight and others are true hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because there are too many rear-runners for the shape to accommodate — none of them is likely to pressure Water Of Leith early, reinforcing a single-paced, uncontested lead. With one horse able to bowl along unchallenged and set its own rhythm, the race will likely be run at a fair but not fierce tempo, leaving Water Of Leith with energy reserves late and making it difficult for genuine hold-up horses to generate the finishing surge they need. This shape strongly favours horses who can track the leader in a close-up position and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — a prominent or close-stalking style is the profile to be on, with pure closers at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Water Of Leith Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith secures an unchallenged lead and controls the tempo throughout without any rival willing to pressurise.
scenarios.body: Water Of Leith sets a fair but manageable gallop, denies rivals a true test and holds on as the field fails to close in the final furlong on fast ground; close-tracking horses who can latch onto the leader are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sufficient to set up a genuine finish and horses tracking Water Of Leith from second or third can collar it inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse tucked just off the leader throughout benefits from the even gallop and produces a decisive late half-furlong run; those with recent good-ground form over 6f are ideally equipped.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith goes off too hard for the conditions and ties up inside the final furlong, opening the door for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: The compressed finishing straight at Ayr can produce a late rush if a collapse at the front creates a gap; however, Cotai Starlight, Joshuas Dream and Falcon Queen are all redistributed types who may not secure the wide, clean run they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling disrupts positions, Water Of Leith is pressured off its stride and the race degenerates into a messy sprint with no horse getting a clear passage.
scenarios.body: A chaotic race with multiple switches and checks in running could scramble the result entirely; lower-weighted younger horses like Lanarra or Great Profit with raw ability might benefit from a fortunate passage.

watchPoints.text: Water Of Leith — if it misses the break or is pressed into a pace duel from an unexpected source, the entire race shape collapses and the scenario probabilities shift dramatically toward late closers.

Tap Dancer — Paul Mulrennan rides a horse whose last five starts were all over 7f-10f, making it an obvious non-stayer risk at 6f; if it blows up early it could cause interference to runners tracking close.

Falcon Queen — headgear (hood) is listed and Tom Eaves may ride it more prominently than its natural style suggests; any unexpected forward move could inject pace into what is projected to be a controlled lead scenario.

Lanarra and Great Profit — both 3-year-olds with the lightest weights in the field; on fast ground over 6f at Ayr, weight allowances can be meaningful and either could outrun their odds if the pace is honest enough to set up a late challenge.

Jim Goldie runs four horses in this race (Kelpie Grey, Water Of Leith, Joshuas Dream, Tap Dancer) — stable form is 4/40 in the 14-day window, a moderate but not negligible strike rate, and the yard's tactical preference with multiple runners is worth monitoring in terms of which is ridden to win.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forbidden Colours
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse for Ed Walker whose last four runs show a consistent pattern of racing from the rear; sim-going record is modest (0W0P), and at 44 days since last run, Kieran Shoemark will need to produce a perfectly timed challenge — but in a race not truly set up for closers, the tactical situation is against her.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, Katie Scott's three-year-old will have a clear lead from the gate; sim-going figures are limited but the uncontested pace is the key asset here, and her light weight of 123lbs could prove an advantage in a race she controls.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes the ride on Jim Goldie's four-year-old who has an outstanding record over 7f on good ground (3W in similar conditions), and while he races from hold-up, his powerful winning pattern suggests he can deliver a sustained late run if the fractions allow — the real question is whether the pace is strong enough to set him up.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up specialist who has won twice over this course and trip in good going, but Connor Beasley will need luck in running from his repositioned midfield slot; fresh off a run just seven days ago, fitness is not the concern, but the race shape is.

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner in the field (OR 76), Roaring Ralph's prominent style sits perfectly against Carmel Valley's lone front-running role; the blinkered six-year-old has two course wins and has been placed five times in similar conditions, and Mark Winn on board is a cool tactical rider who will know exactly where to sit.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old has posted three consecutive thirds and is consistent but limited — Jake Dickson's 5lb claim narrows the weight disadvantage, and good-to-firm Ayr form is solid, but a hold-up style in a race lacking a strong enough gallop to generate meaningful pace figures makes a deep late run difficult to envisage.

races.paceDynamic: Carmel Valley is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and will stride to the front unchallenged from the off, setting a sustainable, controlled gallop over this 7f at Ayr on good-to-firm ground. With no rival likely to press for the lead, this is a race where the pace will be honest but not scorching, meaning the tempo is set entirely on Carmel Valley's terms with the field strung out behind at a measured clip. Roaring Ralph, prominent by style, will track closely in second, while the hold-up contingent — Native Honey, Abduction, Forbidden Colours, and Imperial Guard — will settle in behind with cover. This shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers and those who can travel close to a controlled pace, as the lack of genuine pressure means those waiting for a true end-to-end gallop to deliver late momentum will find the race doesn't truly set up for a sweeping finish. Note that the field contains more hold-up types than can all find their natural position at the rear, with Forbidden Colours and Imperial Guard redistributed to midfield on the map — those who actually secure the prominent slots close to Carmel Valley hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Carmel Valley Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Carmel Valley is allowed to roll along at her own pace and no rival applies early pressure, rewarding horses who travel close to the tempo.
scenarios.body: Carmel Valley sets a controlled, comfortable fractions with Roaring Ralph in her slipstream, and the lack of genuine competition for the lead means the race becomes a test of cruising speed rather than finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph travels powerfully into second and edges closer to Carmel Valley in the straight, turning the race into a match between the two lead-prominent runners.
scenarios.body: Roaring Ralph's solid recent winning form and experience at the trip gives him the tools to reel in Carmel Valley once they turn for home, with the gap to the hold-up horses already too large to bridge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected and the hold-up horses are delivered with a well-timed run from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Native Honey and Imperial Guard, both proven winners over this track and trip in similar going, would be the most likely beneficiaries if a true gallop opens up ground for late closers — though the redistributed positioning of Forbidden Colours and Imperial Guard makes this scenario less reliable than form alone suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Early
scenarios.trigger: If Carmel Valley stumbles, misses the break, or an unforeseen incident scrambles the early order.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early phase would nullify the pace map entirely and hand the initiative to whoever reacts quickest, likely benefiting Roaring Ralph who is already primed to race prominently and has the class to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Carmel Valley's early sectionals are critical — if she dawdles in the first two furlongs she will be caught in the closing stages by Roaring Ralph before the hold-up horses can close.
Roaring Ralph ran just three days ago; while trainer Michael Dods has a solid 14-day record (4/27), watch for signs of fatigue late in the straight given the quick turnaround.

Native Honey and Imperial Guard are both hold-up types who have won over this exact course and trip — if either gets a clean passage through the two-furlong marker, do not dismiss a late surge even against the race shape.

Forbidden Colours and Imperial Guard, both redistributed in the pace map, are true closers squeezed into midfield roles; if either attempts to push forward to find a better position, it could disrupt the clean tactical picture and compress the early pace.

Weight differential is notable — Carmel Valley carries 123lbs against Roaring Ralph's 142lbs and Native Honey's 138lbs — on a flat, fast track over 7f, that 15-19lb swing in favour of the front-runner is worth monitoring against the prominent and hold-up rivals in the closing stages.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Get More With Ladbucks' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Samra Star
runners_data.note: Lightly raced mare returning from 67 days off for Linda Perratt, with modest sim-going form (0 wins, 1 place from 15 runs); her true running style is deep hold-up, but the crowded rear means she will likely be shuffled into a midfield position she is not entirely comfortable with, limiting her ability to deliver a clean late run.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Nature
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner absent a significant 321 days and returning cold off a long break, which is a major concern; rated just OR 51 and her three-run career form on similar going reads only 0W1P from 3, and though she is a natural hold-up type she will be pressed further forward than ideal in this shape.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Lively each-way angle after winning twice on Good going at 8f (Ayr form included), trained by Jim Goldie who is 4/40 over 14 days but the horse herself is clearly in form (1-4-1 in recent starts); she is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination but has the tactical versatility to race closer, making her one of the few redistributed types who could legitimately operate in a prominent role.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Won at 9f on Good going last time and is lightly penalised at OR 63; headgear note (p — previously ran prominently) and his hg:p tag suggests he has the profile to race more handy, and at just 7 days since his last run he arrives race-fit — one of the more dangerous of the redistributed hold-up horses if he secures a prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with solid placed form at 6-7f on Soft but stepping up to 1m on Good today, and sim-going figures read only 0W1P from 15 — the step up to this trip is a query; a natural hold-up horse who will be nudged into a midfield position in this shape, reducing his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Keats House
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, carrying the visor (hg:v) and ridden by Tom Eaves for the Easterby yard; recent form reads five defeats including consecutive 5th-7th placings, but his tactical role as sole pace-setter means he will enjoy an uncontested lead — the key question is whether his form figures (12 runs on similar going, 1W5P) reflect a horse who can convert that advantage.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form — won at 8f on Good and placed at 8f on Good twice more, accumulating 1W4P from 7 runs on sim-going; trained by Tristan Davidson (3/12 over 14 days) and ridden by Jason Hart, he is a true hold-up horse but has the class edge at OR 65 and the finishing form to be dangerous from wherever he ends up in the field.

runners_data.name: Eeetee
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old carrying 141lbs with a bleak recent form string of 8-7-8-10-8 including a blank on similar going (1W2P from 9 but that win appears historic); headgear note (p) and the age suggest a horse in decline, and OR 64 is unlikely to be competitive given this evidence — hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Union Island
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner (2/41 over 14 days is modest) on a course where he finished 6th last time at 8f on Standard; sim-going figures read 1W2P from 6, reasonable but not compelling, and at OR 63 he is mid-pack in the weights — a hold-up horse who will need a strong pace to be delivered into contention, which this race shape is unlikely to provide.

races.paceDynamic: Keats House is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mile handicap on Good to Firm ground at Ayr, and with no genuine rival to press him from the front, he is set to dictate a controlled, measured pace from the outset. The absence of pressure means he can switch off in front and conserve energy, making his sectionals through the first half-mile highly likely to be moderate — this is a pace scenario that historically benefits horses who can track the leader and deploy a sustained finishing effort rather than those who need to make up ground from far back. The field contains a significant cluster of hold-up performers — Samra Star, Spirit Of Nature, Approaching Dawn, Mayor Of Maghera, and Novak are all redistributed in the map because true rear-of-field positions are oversubscribed; in reality, several of these will be forced wider and closer than they want, with Approaching Dawn and Mayor Of Maghera the most likely to actually press into prominent territory given their recent form profiles. This race shape strongly favours a stalking, prominent-to-midfield profile that can cover the modest pace and pounce in the final two furlongs rather than a deep hold-up horse dependent on a strong gallop to deliver them into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keats House Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Keats House is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop that keeps runners bunched and unwilling to commit.
scenarios.body: Keats House controls the tempo from stall to home turn, turning a potentially flat pace into a test of finishing speed over the final two furlongs; horses that have tracked him closely throughout are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third off Keats House's steady pace produces a sharp turn of foot in the final furlong to wear him down.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop compresses the field into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, and any horse with a high TS who has avoided traffic by sitting handy is ideally placed; this is a straightforward overtaking exercise for a natural prominent type.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens genuinely from halfway, stretching the field and creating daylight for a late-running horse to find a clear passage.
scenarios.body: A genuine increase in tempo through the back straight would suit those redistributed horses who manage to get closer than their natural rear-of-field position suggests; Approaching Dawn's recent Ayr win at this trip and distance makes her the principal beneficiary if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse Of Front-Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Keats House's low recent form (0 wins from 12 on similar going, five consecutive disappointing efforts) results in his uncontested lead evaporating after the home turn.
scenarios.body: A faltering leader would compress the finish into a scramble, handing advantage to whichever prominent horse has tracked most efficiently and has enough residual energy to pick up; the low-mileage, lightly-raced Union Island and the rejuvenated Runninsonofagun would profit most.

watchPoints.text: Keats House sets a genuinely uncontested pace — watch whether Tom Eaves elects to exploit this fully by going clear early, because if he does the entire field faces a flat-footed sprint finish that could catch hold-up horses cold.

Mayor Of Maghera, Approaching Dawn and Novak are all oversubscribed for the few available prominent-to-midfield positions — watch the first two furlongs for a positional squeeze that could force one or more of them wider or further back than intended, disrupting their race entirely.

Spirit Of Nature is returning from 321 days off with no public trial — watch her in the pre-parade ring for any signs of physical fitness concern; a cold return at this distance for Jim Goldie is a significant risk flag.

Runninsonofagun ran just seven days ago — watch whether he shows any signs of residual fatigue in the closing stages, as a horse who has already had a hard race this week may not find his usual finish under a patient Jason Hart ride.

The going report consistently lists this race as Good to Firm despite the race card showing Good — watch the official going board at the course before betting, as a firmer surface would favour Keats House's front-running style even more decisively.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rastnet
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner here with back-to-back placed efforts over this trip on Soft and Standard, and his sim-going record on Good is thin (1 run, placed); Beasley is an astute front-runner's partner and 44 days off is a minor watch point, but the solo lead role is a genuine tactical asset — his STYLE_FIT tag warns he is already operating at the edge of a comfortable role if pressed.

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4-year-old has an excellent similar-going profile (13 from 15 place efforts on Good) and returns after just 18 days, suggesting sharpness; his natural hold-up habit means he may need to adjust forward in the absence of a true pace, and his lack of a win since is a concern, but his consistency and going record make him a solid each-way profile.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6-year-old has won twice on Good over this general trip range and finished third most recently, returning in 14 days in good order; her hold-up style means she is dependent on the front end coming back to her, but on fast ground where the gallop can stay honest enough, she is a live finisher with proven form at the trip.

runners_data.name: Colourband
runners_data.note: The Simon & Ed Crisford 3-year-old won over 10f on Good and finished second over 8f, suggesting the step back to 1m2f on this going is perfectly timed; 45 days off is notable but the Crisford yard has fired fresh horses successfully, and his prominent style suits a race where Rastnet sets a manageable tempo — a strong candidate for the lead scenario.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen's mount has a near-perfect similar-going record (14/15 on Good) and has placed at 8f and 11f, though the bulk of his form is at 8f and the step up in trip here is a question; 10 days between runs suggests he is in a productive spell and Jim Goldie runs him alongside stablemates, which occasionally leads to team tactics worth noting.

runners_data.name: Empirical
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3-year-old won over 8f on Good last time and clearly has ability, but his natural front-running instincts place him in the redistributed midfield here given the prominent slots are taken; Shoemark is strong enough to push for position, yet racing outside his comfort zone at a first try over 1m2f for a trainer in fair current form adds two layers of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old with three wins from his last five at 11-12f on Good, Alpine Sierra is clearly at home over this trip and going, but his tendency to want to race prominently has him mapped out of position in a race already carrying front-end traffic; Lauren Young claims 5lb which helps the weight, yet the combination of age, redistribution, and having to settle deeper than usual makes this a tough ask despite the rock-solid trip-and-going profile.

races.paceDynamic: Rastnet is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outside, Connor Beasley can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Ayr. Obito and Colourband are the natural prominent rivals, but neither is a confirmed pace-setter, meaning Rastnet is unlikely to be seriously pressured early and can dictate the fractions. Empirical and Alpine Sierra are genuine prominent types by nature but both have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the prominent berths are already occupied — they will either have to push for a position they may not get or race in an unnatural role, discounting their pure chance. This race shape — a controlled single leader, modest early tempo on fast ground over a middle distance — strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace without burning energy, then produce a clean sustained finish, making prominent-to-midfield closers with good form on similar going the primary profile to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rastnet Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Rastnet is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a comfortable, even gallop that denies closers a true target to aim at.
scenarios.body: Beasley dictates every yard at a tempo that suits a lone front-runner, and the Good to Firm surface rewards horses who can maintain rhythm rather than produce a single surge late. Prominent-travelling types who can latch onto Rastnet turning in — particularly Obito and Colourband — are best placed, with Pearl Eye the main danger from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fire Late
scenarios.trigger: If Obito or Colourband tracks Rastnet closely enough to pounce in the final two furlongs as the pace-setter ties up.
scenarios.body: With a modest gallop set by Rastnet, horses that have travelled prominently throughout arrive at the two-furlong pole with energy in reserve and the race run to their tempo. Colourband's win at this trip on Good ground and Obito's strong similar-going record of 13/15 place efforts make both live contenders in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the front-runner ties up badly, creating a gap for Pearl Eye or Geo to motor through from the rear.
scenarios.body: Pearl Eye has won twice over this trip on Good ground and Jim Goldie's yard is in form; a soft lead pace that sets up a strong final quarter-mile suits her profile perfectly. Geo is a consistent track-and-trip performer with 14 from 15 on similar going but has been scoring mainly over shorter and may not quite get to the principals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Pair Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If Empirical or Alpine Sierra aggressively fight for prominent ground and inject enough pace to scramble the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Both are natural prominent types forced wider in the map by a crowded front end, and if either forces their way into position it burns energy and lifts the tempo, potentially suiting a different closer. However, their out-of-role starting point makes this the least likely scenario, and the STYLE_FIT tags on both horses temper confidence in their ability to win a race run outside their natural rhythm.

watchPoints.text: Colourband — a prominent-style 3-year-old from a powerful Crisford yard returning after 45 days; if he travels fluently just off Rastnet's shoulder, he is the most dangerous horse to the leader in the final two furlongs.

Empirical and Alpine Sierra — both are natural prominent racers mapped to midfield; watch the early stages to see if either jockey tries to push forward, as fighting for position could inject pace and unsettle the controlled race shape Rastnet needs.

Pearl Eye — Goldie's hold-up mare has the best trip-and-going profile in the field; if the pace is even slightly stronger than anticipated and the front end ties up, she will be finishing fastest of all and could appear late at long odds.

Geo — back in just 10 days suggesting peak fitness, and his near-perfect Good-going record is striking; he is shorter in trip than ideal here, so watch whether he travels easily in the back straight or gets outpaced when the race quickens, as that will tell you immediately whether the 1m2f is within range.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for John Wainwright and Jason Hart, with five recent runs at 5f on Good ground returning zero wins but two places; comes in on just nine days' rest and needs a clear late run which this compressed, front-runner-dominated shape makes difficult to find.

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type trained by Linda Perratt and partnered by Connor Beasley, whose recent form includes a win at 5f on Standard and a placed effort on Good; has the finishing kick to feature but is entirely dependent on getting a clean passage from the rear in a packed midfield.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Jim Goldie and Mark Winn, and the key pace-shaper of the entire race; a headgear flag (h) is noted and her 10 runs on similar ground with one win and five places signals genuine affinity for today's conditions — dictating an uncontested lead is her optimum scenario.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly for Iain Jardine and Andrew Mullen who won last time out over 5f on Good and has the freshest winning form in the field after a 35-day break; capable of a bold show if she can reproduce that effort, though her six-furlong form on Soft is a lesser pointer for this sharp flat 5f.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner also trained by Jim Goldie carrying a visor (v), who is the most natural partner to Wee Mary in the early stages; a recent course win over 6f on Good and consistent placed form over 5f at Ayr make him the most likely beneficiary if Wee Mary weakens late — his natural tracking position is genuinely advantageous here.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Consistent five-year-old who genuinely wants to come from off the pace — placed in midfield on the map because the field simply holds too many hold-up types to place them all at the rear; his best form tends to come over 5-6f on Good with some pace to chase, and the likely front-runner-dominated shape here does not play to his strengths, tempering his prospects.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Six-year-old mare for trainer R Mike Smith whose true instinct is to hold up and finish late — mapped to midfield because the race cannot accommodate all the closers at the back; a recent runner-up over 6f on Good shows she retains ability, but the uncontested pace from Wee Mary keeps late finishers at a structural disadvantage today.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old hold-up type, placed into midfield on the map as the race holds more closers than can all settle at the rear; her recent runs have been over 6-7f on Good and Soft, making this drop to 5f on Good-to-Firm a notable trip and ground query that further limits her claims.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran for Linda Perratt who is a natural closer but finds himself in a crowded midfield group for shape reasons rather than by inclination; four places from his last five runs at 5f on Good show he competes well in this grade, but without a strong pace to close into he rarely wins — one to respect for a place only.

races.paceDynamic: Wee Mary is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 5f handicap and, crucially, she faces no genuine pace pressure — the field behind her is stacked with hold-up types, meaning she can stride into a comfortable lead from the outset and control every yard of this race at a sustainable tempo. Doon The Glen is the only other natural prominent racer and may attempt to track Wee Mary closely, but with Jim Goldie running both horses there is no incentive for a burning duel. The bulk of the field — Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Summerstorms Dream, Sixcor, Startling, Henery Hawk and Supremissy — are all genuine hold-up performers, and with so many closers unable to secure their natural rear positions, several will be shuffled into a congested midfield pack that is neither here nor there tactically. On Good to Firm ground over a flat 5f at Ayr, a steady-to-moderate pace set by an uncontested leader almost always rewards those who travel prominently and pick up efficiently in the final two furlongs rather than those making ground from off the pace; this race shape therefore favours Wee Mary and any horse that tracks her closely — prominently-placed runners who avoid the midfield scrimmage hold the structural edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wee Mary Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wee Mary leads in isolation and the pace stays measured, she dictates throughout on her terms.
scenarios.body: With no pace rival to push her beyond a sustainable tempo, Wee Mary can conserve enough to find extra in the final furlong on this flat course; her Good-to-Firm record of 10 runs with a win and five places on that surface underlines her aptitude for today's conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Doon The Glen tracks Wee Mary tightly and the front-runner ties up near home, a close tracker delivers the winning blow.
scenarios.body: Doon The Glen has won over 6f at Ayr and has solid form on Good ground; sitting a length off the leader throughout the race puts him in an ideal position to exploit any late fade from Wee Mary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely brisk enough to compromise the leaders and the hold-up pack finds a clear run, a strong finisher gets up.
scenarios.body: Supremissy won last time out over 5f on Good and has the profile to finish fastest of all if the race is run at a punishing clip; Startling and Henery Hawk also carry genuine late pace but need gaps to appear in a compressed midfield.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Turns Chaotic
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling disrupts Wee Mary's rhythm and the field fractures into a scrimmage with no clear leader, an opportunist prevails.
scenarios.body: A messy race with multiple positional changes on the flat 5f at Ayr would scramble the expected order and could elevate a horse like Sixcor or Henery Hawk who have consistent placed form in similar conditions; both have shown they can run competitive races when the dynamic is unsettled.

watchPoints.text: Wee Mary lands unopposed in front at the first stride — if she clears the early exchanges without challenge from Doon The Glen, the race is effectively hers to lose and the entire field is chasing her tail.

Doon The Glen and Wee Mary are both trained by Jim Goldie and run under the same connections — watch for any stable tactics that might see Doon The Glen deliberately restrained rather than pressing his stablemate for the lead.

The five redistributed hold-up horses (Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Summerstorms Dream, Sixcor and Startling/Henery Hawk) will converge into a tight midfield pack; significant traffic and interference in the final two furlongs is a genuine risk for any of them trying to finish.

Supremissy arrives on a 35-day break having won last time out — freshness combined with a hold-up style means she needs everything to fall right, but a market move in the ring would signal stable confidence worth noting.

Good to Firm official going confirmed for this 5f race — any further drying during the afternoon card could sharpen the surface and bring Wee Mary's front-running profile into even sharper focus, so check the going report update before the off.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Royal Blaze
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner whose hold on the lead looks uncontested; five-year-old in tongue-tie returned 21 days ago, Whillans stable in decent 14-day form, and good ground is confirmed fine — the danger is the step up in field size testing ability to control tempo throughout.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes the ride for Jim Goldie on this hold-up mare who has been knocking at the door in a similar grade; six-year-old's recent form at 8-10f on good/soft hasn't yielded a win since her form string tailed off, and the 10f trip here may be her minimum stretch.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer for Jim Goldie who is right in her element at around 1m1f-1m3f on good ground, finishing placed in four of her last five over 11-13f; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a genuine advantage and 14 days since her last run looks fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has spent his recent career racing over marathon trips (16f+), making this 10f trip a significant step down in distance; blinkers applied, Jardine yard modest in 14-day strike rate, and the drop in trip may leave him underpowered in the finish.

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been consistently placed at 10f on good ground, including a second last time out; Kieran Shoemark is a major jockey upgrade, blinkers retained, and racing just seven days after his last run suggests fitness is peak — well placed tactically if Annandale and Royal Blaze set it up.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who wants a thorough test, with all five recent runs over 12f or further; the drop to 10f is a concern given she needs a strong gallop to get involved, and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is the main positive in an otherwise modest booking.

runners_data.name: Betty Bassett
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up filly who has been running in shorter 8f handicaps on standard ground; all her placed efforts have come on all-weather, the turf form shows nothing encouraging, and 42 days off combined with a trainer showing 0-from-3 in the past fortnight limits appeal.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield position on the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with closers; Philip Kirby runner won last time at 10f on good ground and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable — the tactical question is whether he finds clear running from his constrained position.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 8f on good ground and Jason Hart is an experienced pilot, but this Christopher Kellett runner is a natural hold-up type who won't naturally find the prominent berth the map shows him in; his best form has come over shorter trips, and the 10f trip here is at the upper limit of his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Lightning Galaxy
runners_data.note: Consistent underperformer in recent form — five runs reading 0-9-9-5-9 — suggesting this Michael Dods four-year-old is not firing at present; tongue-tie applied, Connor Beasley has strong course form at Ayr, but the horse's natural position at the rear makes it hard to win from here with that level of recent output.

runners_data.name: One More Bottle
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh returns this five-year-old after a lengthy 198-day absence, the longest layoff in the field; all her career form has been on all-weather, and the step onto turf on good-to-firm ground on her first run back makes her essentially unknown quantity here.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old gelding who showed a rare placed effort three runs ago at 8f on good ground; James Sullivan takes over, but the horse's age, inconsistent recent form across 8-10f, and a low OR of 48 suggest he needs everything to fall right to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's six-year-old has not won in recent turf form and the last five runs show only minor placed efforts; natural hold-up style is compressed further by the field's depth of closers, and a poor recent showing on good ground at 10f last time offers limited encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Blaze is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 1m2f handicap, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Ewan Whillans' five-year-old should be able to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground at Ayr. Falcon Nine and Annandale are the most likely prominent trackers, sitting just off Royal Blaze and creating a modest pace scenario rather than a truly pressured one. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Recobella, Daring Leader, Lightning Galaxy, One More Bottle, Golden Valour and Zebra Star all prefer to come from off the pace, yet many are mapped to midfield because the genuine rear slots are oversubscribed; of these, Recobella and Daring Leader have the strongest recent form and are most likely to push furthest forward from that group. A controlled, single-pace gallop on fast ground at a track where the straight is relatively short favours horses sitting prominently in behind the leader, able to respond without needing a long run — off-the-pace types relying on a late sprint face a much sterner challenge given the modest tempo this shape produces.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Blaze Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Blaze secures the lead uncontested and sets a steady, metronomic gallop throughout the 1m2f.
scenarios.body: Royal Blaze dictates every yard, burns off little energy, and kicks from the front in the straight on ground that suits; horses prominent just behind — Falcon Nine and Annandale — are ideally placed to pounce if he ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Falcon Nine and Annandale track Royal Blaze closely and one outfinishes him in a sprint for the line.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest enough to keep Royal Blaze honest but not so fierce that the prominent pair are cooked; Falcon Nine's recent second at 10f on good ground and Kieran Shoemark's big-race experience make him the stand-out profile here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to open the race up and a hold-up horse gets a clear run through in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Recobella and Daring Leader both won last time out and have the recent form to capitalise if the tempo genuinely quickens early and leaves the front two vulnerable; however, both are mapped forward of their natural position, meaning this scenario depends partly on them finding room from a constrained midfield berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Blaze is pressured unexpectedly or fades sharply, leaving a chaotic final-furlong scramble.
scenarios.body: Just Dottie or Penelope's Sister, both patient hold-up mares with good-ground form, could benefit from a messy finish if the race fragments; the low probability reflects that this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously in a race that looks straightforward in shape.

watchPoints.text: Royal Blaze sets the entire pace shape — watch whether Falcon Nine or Annandale press him immediately out of the gates, because any early pressure could blow the race wide open and undermine the dominant front-running scenario.

Recobella and Daring Leader both carry race-winning form but are mapped into midfield away from their natural hold-up positions — watch for potential traffic issues in the straight if the field compresses, which could cost either a clean run.

Annandale has been competitive over longer trips (11-13f) but steps down to 10f here — watch if she finds the trip sharp, particularly if Royal Blaze sets a modest pace that fails to stretch her stamina advantage.
One More Bottle returns from 198 days off and has no turf form to speak of — watch early to see if she settles or pulls, as either could distort the race shape from the rear of the field.

The going report consistently reads Good To Firm for this race despite the nominal card description of Good — horses with proven fast-ground form, particularly Royal Blaze and Falcon Nine, carry an extra edge that should be factored into any assessment of the pace dynamic.
